cases.title: Thread Composer Channel Suggestions

summary: Channel suggestion list is vertically split/duplicated on Android: appears at top of viewport AND near vertical middle, instead of positioned above the composer toolbar as in React.
React shows the suggestions list in the lower half of the canvas, immediately above the composer action bar; Android renders the same list near the top of the screen.
React composer toolbar sits directly under the suggestions list as one stacked group; Android shows a large empty gap between the suggestions list and the composer action bar.
Suggestions list content (# design selected, # product, # android-artifacts) is identical between platforms — only positioning/vertical offset differs.
0.20% pixel-perfect similarity and 99.8% mismatch confirm a wholesale layout translation, not a subtle style delta.
likelyCauses: Android suggestion popup anchor or offset is using a wrong anchor view (e.g., attaching to root/Activity instead of the composer EditText).
Suggestions component is being rendered twice or in two different parents (e.g., inside both the toolbar container and the main content view).
Different vertical centering/anchor logic between React (popup over composer) and Android (popup top-anchored to screen).
Crop on Android uses x=24 offset which may exclude left padding, indicating the suggestion bounds themselves are mis-positioned relative to the composer.
Missing bottom-anchored CoordinatorLayout/AppBar offset that React's absolute-positioned popover provides.
suggestedFixes: Anchor the suggestions PopupWindow/AnchorView to the composer EditText with PopUpPositionBuilder.alignToBottomEdge() so it floats directly above the composer.
Remove duplicate render path — ensure the suggestions list is only added to the composer container, not the activity root.
Match React's popover offset: top of suggestions list should sit ~8dp above the composer toolbar with no gap in between.
Recapture the screenshot with the crop rect at x=0 (not x=24) so the suggestion list bounds align with the composer's horizontal bounds for fair diffing.
Add a Slock visual regression test for channel-suggestions with the popup-open state to prevent regressions.

Send (paper plane) button on iOS sits inside a visible pink/coral square fill, whereas on React the button background blends more subtly with the row.
Typography weight of channel names ('design', 'product', 'android-artifacts') looks heavier/bolder on iOS versus React's lighter weight.
likelyCauses: iOS implementation missing explicit top inset/padding on the suggestions container
iOS row header not rendering the hashtag badge background tile (icon asset or container style regression)
Platform-specific font weight mapping causing iOS to use a heavier SF/system variant than React's web font

suggestedFixes: Add equivalent top padding/inset on the iOS channel suggestions container to match React's vertical rhythm
Restore the yellow '#' badge background tile on the iOS composer row header (check icon asset and view background)
Align iOS channel name font weight with the React design token (e.g., semibold → medium)

summary: The iOS canvas is much taller (1170×2532 vs 342×320 baseline crop), making the channel-suggestions block sit in the upper portion with a large empty area below rather than the compact Android layout.

Highlight/selection color token mapped to a different pink shade on iOS.
Container layout using raw pixel measurements on one platform and dp on the other.

Vertical padding/density tokens differ between platforms, inflating row and overall list height.

cases.title: Thread Message Row Deleted Human

summary: Recipient name text differs in weight: React renders 'Former Teammate' as bold; Android renders 'Designer' as regular/non-bold weight.
State badge label differs: React shows 'REMOVED', Android shows 'DELETED'.
Timestamp format differs: React displays '06/22 03:10 AM' (12-hour with AM); Android displays '06/26 17:15' (24-hour, no AM/PM).
Typography size appears slightly larger on the Android side for the recipient name and message body, giving the Android row a denser visual stack.

Avatar badge on Android is rendered in a desaturated/muted tone (greyer) versus React's more saturated lavender fill, indicating the deleted-author state styling is applied but with a different palette intensity.
likelyCauses: Platform-specific copy/state mapping: Android component maps the deleted-human author state to a 'DELETED' label instead of the design-system 'REMOVED' label used in React.
Locale/time-format divergence: Android uses a 24-hour locale formatter, React uses a 12-hour AM/PM formatter.
Typography stack mismatch between platforms leads to different font weights and line-height for the author name and message body.
Bottom-padded reactions row was not re-measured for the Android font metrics, causing overflow/clipping at the component bounds.
suggestedFixes: Normalize the deleted-author state badge label to 'REMOVED' (or update the React baseline to 'DELETED') so both platforms render the same copy.
Use a single shared timestamp formatter (12-hour with AM/PM in en-US) across React and Android.
Align font weight/size for the recipient name and message body with the React baseline, or regenerate the Android baseline using the updated fonts.
Increase the row's min-height or bottom padding on Android so the reactions row is not clipped when font metrics differ.
Verify the avatar's muted/deleted color token on Android matches the React muted-lavender swatch.
intentional: Timestamp format change to 24-hour may be intentional locale behavior on Android and should be confirmed with design.

State-mapping mismatch: Android titlebar component is wired to a different state (e.g., error) than React for the same props.

Background color difference suggests Android activity/theme uses a different surface color than React.

intentional: The cream Android background may be an intentional Material/Android surface color if the design system specifies platform-specific surfaces.

Map Android body text style to the same font weight used by React for notification descriptions.

cases.title: Home Search Results

summary: Result count and result set differ: React shows '3 RESULTS' with one channel result and two message results; Android shows '5 results' with two entity results (channel + DM) and three message results, plus a 'Load more results' button.

Filter row layout divergence: React renders a two-row wrapping chip group including 'Recent' sort chip and 'Clear All'; Android renders a single non-wrapping row with fewer, fully-populated filter chips (From: Me, Scope 2, #design). Documented as intentional platform difference.
DM/Agent result card present on Android only: 'Android Developer' DM card with 'Agent · @Android-Developer · Members' subline has no counterpart on React.

Channel result metadata differs: React's 'android-artifacts' row shows just 'Channel'; Android adds a 'Builds and screenshots' description line and uses different label placement for the 'Channel' tag.

Message card timestamps and structure differ: React uses relative time ('20 days ago'); Android uses clock timestamps (10:38, 10:31, 09:58) and one message carries a 'Thread #design 2 hits' header with a pink/highlighted background, which is absent on React.
likelyCauses: Search API response size or pagination state differs between React and Android clients (Android fetched additional entities and messages).
Filter chip component uses different wrapping/count policies per platform, producing different result-set previews.
Locale/time formatting differs: React formats relative dates, Android formats absolute HH:MM.
DM entity result type is rendered on Android but not yet implemented or filtered out on React.
Threaded-message variant with hits-summary header is a React-not-yet-adopted component currently shipping on Android.
suggestedFixes: Reconcile result-set contract: ensure both clients paginate and aggregate channel, DM, and message results identically; add a shared fixtures/contract test.
Unify filter chip behavior to a documented platform rule and surface the same active filter set on both sides (or accept divergence in design system).
Pick one timestamp formatting (relative vs absolute) or align by platform rules so both sides read consistently.
Add the DM/Agent result card to the React search results list, or explicitly exclude DM entity results on both platforms.
Decide on the threaded-message-with-hits card: either back-port to React or document as Android-only and update visual baselines.
intentional: Filter chip row count, wrap, and presence of the sort/Recent chip differs between React (multi-row) and Android (single row) — intentional mobile-vs-web platform divergence mirroring tasks.panel filter-row declaration.

cases.title: Home Search Channel Dropdown

summary: Channel dropdown is open on Android (right) but closed on React (left); React shows a static '# Channel' selector with no flyout, while Android renders an open panel with search input, item list, selected check, and DM entry.

Filter chip row differs: React shows partial chips ('From', 'Scope', 'Channel', 'Any Time', 'Relevant') clipped at left edge with no icons; Android shows fully visible '@ From: Me', '@ Scope 2', '# #design' chips on a yellow filled background plus a back arrow icon in the search bar.

Selected channel indicator is missing on Android (no 'android-artifacts selected' CHANN... badge) and Android instead shows a small inline checkmark next to '#design' in the dropdown, while React has a yellow left bar on the selected row.

Main content area layout diverges: React renders a left-aligned 'RESULTS / CHANNELS & DMS' header and message cards clipped to the left half of the viewport; Android renders full-width cards with avatars, timestamps, thread indicators, and a 'Load more results' button.
Primary search action differs: React search input has a clear (×) icon button on the right; Android replaces it with a back arrow on the left and omits the inline clear button.

Different filter chip specs between platforms — Android uses filled yellow chips with full labels and icons; React uses outlined chips with truncated labels and no prefix icons.

Result list rendering is built from different components per platform: Android pulls MessageItem/ThreadMessageItem with avatars, timestamps, and a Load more action; React renders a simplified card list without those affordances.

Unify filter chip design — same filled vs outlined treatment, full label visibility, and leading '@' / '#' icons in both React and Android.
Normalize search input accessory: pick one (back arrow or clear button) and apply consistently across platforms.
Reuse the shared MessageItem/ThreadMessageItem component on React (or add a React equivalent) so author, avatar, timestamp, thread badge, and Load more appear identically.
Define a shared design token set for chip background color, selected-row indicator, card padding, and avatar size to enforce parity.

Channel dropdown component implementation diverges between platforms (different header items, different result list contents, missing back navigation on web).

analysis.suggestedOwner: Design Systems / Search component owner (cross-platform parity)
suggestedFixes: Capture both screenshots in matching states (same query, same selected filters, dropdown open with same result set) before diffing.
Fix React layout so the search header and filters are not clipped on the left — verify min-width / overflow handling for the 390px viewport.
Add the back-arrow affordance to React header, or intentionally document/remove it from iOS, so navigation parity is explicit.

intentional: Difference in raw canvas size (React 390×844 vs iOS 1170×2532) — expected, since Slock scales for comparison.
Platform-native icons (search glyph, back arrow) may intentionally differ in style.

summary: Channel dropdown panel width is slightly wider on iOS than on Android, extending further to the right edge of the viewport.
Dropdown vertical position (top offset) appears slightly lower on iOS relative to the search bar.

likelyCauses: Platform-specific font metrics (SF Pro on iOS vs. Roboto on Android) causing minor kerning and text-run width differences that shift adjacent layout.
Kuikly runtime using platform-default TextMeasurement without explicit line-height/letter-spacing overrides.
AutoLayout/Box being width-constrained by content rather than parent, causing the dropdown to size to the wider iOS text.
suggestedFixes: Constrain the Channel dropdown width to an explicit dp value (e.g., match-parent or fixed 343dp on 390 viewport) instead of wrap-content to align both ends.
Set explicit fontFamily + lineHeight + letterSpacing on filter chip and dropdown item Text components to neutralize OS font substitution.
Verify dropdown top-offset uses the same dp anchor on both platforms; align to a shared design token.
Audit highlight (mark) span padding so its width is identical across platforms.
intentional: Pixel-perfect similarity is 90.42% which is above the 90% acceptable threshold; remaining differences are sub-2dp and likely platform font metrics, not regressions.
Different raw canvas sizes (390×844 vs 1170×2532) explain a portion of the mismatch ratio without indicating a real layout divergence.

summary: Android renders only 3 result cards while React shows a continuously scrolling list of 5+ cards within the same viewport.
Card row heights and internal spacing are taller on Android, causing earlier cards to occupy more vertical space.
Bookmark icon is monochrome/outline on Android vs. filled orange glyph on React.
Avatar tokens differ: 'Product UX Designer' uses a blue square tile on React vs. a multicolored grid glyph on Android; 'artin' avatar token is purple/pink on React vs. muted gray on Android.

likelyCauses: Android implementation is using a larger card paddings/margins or a heavier line-height in the result card typography.
Android bookmark icon is bound to the unfilled/empty state while React binds the filled state.
Android trend tag avatars are sourced from a different token set (channel vs. user) than React.
Relative timestamps in the Android seed render with a different 'days ago' value, suggesting the two builds are not pinned to the same fixture date.
Android paginates the list and renders a 'Load More' CTA; React renders an unpaginated scrollable list.

Switch Android bookmark/bookmark-saved icon to the filled variant matching React's orange glyph.
Normalize the '#design' avatar source to a single token across platforms (channel glyph in both, or user glyph in both).
Pin both baselines to the same fixture timestamps so 'days ago' values are identical and don't shift the header layout.
Remove the 'Load More' button on Android or add the equivalent on React so pagination behavior matches.
intentional: Pagination model may intentionally differ per platform, in which case 'Load More' should be added to the React baseline as well.

summary: Header title row alignment differs: Android adds a checked-checkbox icon to the left of the 'Tasks' title inside the yellow banner; React has no icon and the title sits flush-left.

Task card content ordering differs: Android shows top-right timestamp and bottom-left assignee ('Unassigned', '@Cindy', '@Product UX Designer') on each card; React shows neither — React will adopt these later.

Status pill alignment within task cards is slightly shifted vertically on Android (centered near middle-bottom) versus React (lower-right corner area), due to the added assignee line taking vertical space.

summary: Android 'In Progress' trigger label is rendered with a lighter/thinner font weight than the React baseline (visibly thinner strokes).
Android menu items ('Todo', 'In Progress', 'In Review', 'Done', 'Closed') appear at a slightly larger font size with looser line-height spacing than React.

likelyCauses: Android is using the system default font (e.g., Roboto Regular) instead of the design-system font (e.g., Inter) used in React.
Default TextView/Compose typography style overrides the component's intended size and weight tokens.
Vertical item padding uses a platform-default value (e.g., 16dp) rather than the shared 12dp/14dp design token.
ListItem content padding (end padding for the trailing icon) differs between web and Android implementations.

Override Android text appearance to use the same fontSize tokens as React (e.g., 16sp for trigger, 15sp for items) and explicit lineHeight.
Set the menu item's vertical padding to the shared design token (e.g., 10–12dp) to match React's row height.
Align the trailing checkmark's content padding/end inset with the web implementation (e.g., 16dp).
Re-run the Slock visual test after token updates; the 8% pixel mismatch should drop to near zero.

likelyCauses: Differences in canvas dimensions and device pixel ratio between the React web baseline (342×260) and the iOS snapshot (1170×2532) introduce minor pixel-level mismatches due to scaling.

If differences are confirmed as expected, lower the pixelRatio tolerance or mark this component as intentional in the visual test config.

summary: Menu trigger pill ("In Progress" with edit/pencil icon) and dropdown panel render with matching structure, colors, border weight, and item order on both Android and iOS.

likelyCauses: Minor sub-pixel/anti-aliasing differences in text and icon edges, consistent with the 0.87% pixel mismatch and ~94% RGB similarity.
Slight canvas scaling/resampling difference due to very different raw canvas sizes (342×260 vs 1170×2532) before component crop.
Platform-default text shaping differences (Roboto vs San Francisco) producing marginal glyph metrics within the 1dp layout tolerance.
suggestedFixes: Treat the remaining delta as cosmetic; no action required given 99.13% pixel-perfect similarity.
If a stricter match is desired, normalize text to a single platform-agnostic font (e.g., shared webfont) used identically on Android and iOS Kuikly builds.
Confirm the layoutDp tolerance of 1dp is intentional in the Slock config for this component to avoid future flaky diffs.
Optionally re-crop both ends to identical component bounds (baseline currently uses manual-rect, iOS has no crop) to reduce empty-canvas noise in the metric.
intentional: Identical trigger pill color (cyan) and identical dropdown panel border/shadow style on both platforms.

Button and input component styles specifying fixed pixel heights instead of density-independent values, causing different heights at the 390×844 vs 1170×2532 canvas.
Platform-specific stroke/border thickness defaults being applied differently on iOS.

summary: Inline code spans have visibly different widths between React and Android, causing different wrap points and line break counts for long inline code and paths.
Short inline code segments wrap into more lines on Android (e.g. 'raft.build.markdown.inlineCode' wraps to two lines instead of one; 'go test ./...' breaks separately).
Long path code block wraps to fewer/fatter lines on Android vs React; the React version produces more wrapped lines with a slimmer measurement, Android collapses segments together.

Android task chip rendering for bare #number tokens (e.g. #520) renders as a chip/tag, whereas React renders it as plain text.
likelyCauses: Different inline code measurement / wrapping algorithms between React web and Android Compose TextLayout (e.g. Android breaks at narrower thresholds or uses word-break vs break-word behavior).
Android uses a different default code-span padding or monospace font metrics, increasing per-token measured width.
Known intentional platform difference for bare #number task chips: Android tags all bare #numbers while React only tags resolved refs.
Possible Android message content width differs slightly due to insets/padding or different container padding accounting in thread.MessageRow.
suggestedFixes: Normalize inline code wrapping behavior: align Android's break strategy (e.g. CSS-equivalent overflow-wrap/word-break) with React so long inline code breaks at the same character boundaries.
Tune Android monospace font size / padding for inline code spans to match the React render width, or unify the code span style tokens across platforms.
Verify the message row's content max-width and horizontal padding on Android match React to avoid edge-clipping on long wrapped code.

cases.title: Thread Message Row Markdown Status606

summary: Android message row uses a taller component bounds (390×844) versus React's compact (390×322), introducing large empty cream background below the message content.
Header timestamp and avatar alignment differ: React places avatar tightly beside author name; Android avatar sits lower with a visible gap and the author header line is vertically offset.

Inline token wrapping behavior differs: Android breaks long hex/code tokens mid-string across lines (e.g., 'db01c5e5b91f3696bfda64edde2fc31b3a40ffe9b50881…'), while React keeps the token on fewer lines with different break points.
Markdown emphasis rendering differs: Android shows '@artin' as plain underline without bold/mention highlight, whereas React renders '@artin' in bold with a distinct mention color.
Punctuation and spacing around inline code/highlight chips differ between renders (fullwidth punctuation placement, extra spaces after ':', different line heights).
likelyCauses: Android uses a default ScrollView/ConstraintLayout with a fixed/fillViewport height while React constrains the row to its content height (auto sizing).
Markdown parser/tokenizer on Android splits long unbreakable tokens (hex hashes) using character-level wrapping rules differing from React's CSS word-break behavior.
Missing mention/bold styling tokens in Android's markdown adapter (e.g., Markwon) — '@artin' not recognized as mention, '@' escape producing literal '@'.
Different line-height and font metrics between Android (Roboto) and React (system) leading to vertical alignment drift of the avatar row.
Fullwidth punctuation handling: Android applies CJK punctuation spacing rules differently, causing visible gaps before '：', '，', '。'.
suggestedFixes: Constrain the message row container to wrap_content height (or set a fixed max height matching React's 322dp) so the empty cream area disappears.
Update the Android markdown renderer to apply CSS-style overflow-wrap/word-break so long hex/code tokens wrap at the same boundaries as React, or apply break-word on inline code chips.
Enable mention plugin (or equivalent) in the Android markdown pipeline so '@artin' renders bold with the mention color rather than literal '@' with underline.
Reconcile font family and line-height (e.g., 1.4–1.5) on Android to match React's metrics, and re-center the avatar vertically against the header baseline.
Normalize fullwidth punctuation spacing in the Android text engine or strip trailing whitespace before CJK punctuation to match React output.

cases.title: Settings Connected Apps Full Height Screen

summary: Android adds a top app bar with back arrow and 'Connected Apps' title that is absent in React baseline.
Android duplicates the 'Connected Apps' header as a small icon+label inside the card, while React uses a single uppercase 'CONNECTED APPS' header with a link icon.

Stat cards on Android are repositioned: large numbers (3/2/1) appear stacked above the labels, with the active tab ('Marketplace') highlighted in yellow above the card; React places counts as inline badges next to the tab labels.

Search field is separated on Android into its own 'Marketplace' section with a magnifying-glass icon and sits below a section header; on React the search input is directly under the tab bar in the same card.

App list cards differ: Android collapses GitHub into a two-line description with a pink 'Open' button (uses external-link icon) and uses a white outline 'Details' button with eye icon for Slack Bridge and GitHub Issues; React shows a green 'BUILT-IN' pill, a yellow GitHub avatar tile, 'PRODUCTIVITY' tag, pink 'Install', and green 'INSTALLED' pill.
likelyCauses: Android screen was authored independently and not aligned to the React layout spec.
Section ordering (stats, built-in, marketplace list) was reorganized for the Android variant.
Tab/count UI reimplemented with a different component (vertical stat tiles vs inline count badges).
Different card density and button styling for install/open/detail actions.
Screenshot capture region for Android was cropped shorter, missing footer text.
suggestedFixes: Remove the Android top app bar or hide it when navigating into Connected Apps to match React.
Drop the in-card 'Connected Apps' icon-label header and keep only the uppercase 'CONNECTED APPS' link header.
Restructure stats as inline count badges on the tab buttons (Marketplace 3, Installed 2, My apps 1) rather than stacked numeric tiles.
Move the search input back under the tab bar inside the same card and remove the separate 'Marketplace' section header.
Unify app card layout: yellow square avatar tile, name + subtitle, description, category tag pill, and a single right-aligned action button (Install/Open).
